- [x] **ROUTE-FIND-03 (b): "search"/"look up"/"google" is an explicit websearch command, 2026-09-22 - done 2026-09-22.** **Superseded 2026-09-22:** its wildcard patterns in `websearch/manifest.json` are deleted in D7 (`docs/plans/simple-turn-pipeline-2026-09-22.md`), once the model itself treats a bare "search"/"look up"/"google" as what it already does. "search who won the Seattle Mariners game yesterday" got "Noted.": read against the hub's own logged rows, the model had websearch offered and declined it, and its reply tripped the `placeholder_echo` guard, whose acknowledgment line (`guards.ts`'s `ACKNOWLEDGE`, "Okay."/"Got it."/"Noted.") replaced the cut reply - not, as first read, the remember package's own acknowledgment. `search <anything>` matched nothing in websearch's patterns (`search the web for *`, `search online for *`), so the model was left to decide, and declined; a leading "search" (and "look up", "google") is an explicit websearch command whatever follows, and should never reach the model's discretion at all. Fixed: `backend/packages/websearch/manifest.json` gained `"search *"`, `"look up *"`, `"google *"` patterns (Tier 0, deterministic, always wins, bypassing the model entirely - `turnEngine.ts`'s `routeLiteral()`), which also feeds `commandOpeners()` (routing.ts's `commandOpenersFrom()`) so a search/look-up/google command classifies as a directive and the memory judge skips it, never a fact. Found and fixed along the way: the new bare `"search *"` pattern re-matched text an earlier, more specific pattern had already yielded on for an unresolved reference ("search the web for that movie" with no world head), winning with a wrong, over-broad capture instead of yielding - `routeLiteral()` now makes an unresolved-reference yield skip the rest of that package's patterns entirely, caught by the existing CHAT-13 chunk B test. Also found: `backend/tests/tier2.test.ts`'s invention-retry test used "can you look up the odyssey's rating" as an utterance meant to reach the model (Tier 2), which the new "look up *" pattern now intercepts at Tier 0 - reworded to "can you check the odyssey's rating" (still `REQUEST_RE`-matching, still reaches Tier 2, confirmed with `route()` returning null). Verified: the utterance plus five paraphrases in the routing corpus (`spec/llm/routing-corpus.json`, pinned from `getmaipai/commons` at spec-v0.1.18) with expect `websearch`, a collision pin ("look up the artist Adele" still expects `music`, whose own more specific pattern wins over websearch's new broader one via package iteration order), a `memoryJudge.test.ts` regression proving the judge never treats a search command as a fact, corpus run green with no regression on existing rows, full `bash scripts/check.sh` green (3751 backend + 637 frontend tests, 0 fail). Exit: `bash scripts/check.sh` and the routing corpus bench.

<a id="gate-scope-01"></a>

- [x] **GATE-SCOPE-01: `scripts/check.sh` runs only the stages a diff can touch** (M, owner's rule, org `CLAUDE.md` "Verification" > "Scoped gates", 2026-09-23) - **landed 2026-09-23.** On 2026-09-22 to 23 four sessions landed about thirty mostly frontend-only commits through one four-minute full gate, one at a time, with flaky reruns, each item waiting twenty to sixty minutes from done to live behind a backend suite no frontend file could break. Fixed: `check.sh` reads the working tree against `git merge-base HEAD origin/main` (never literally "the staged diff" - this workflow stages and commits in one step, so nothing is staged at the moment the gate runs, and a staged-only read would fall back to full every time; the org rule's own wording is being corrected to match), classifies the changed paths into `docs`/`frontend`/`backend`/`full` (a new `scripts/gateScope.ts`, unit tested with `bun:test` rather than left as untested bash string matching), and runs only that scope's stages. Rules, in order: a workspace `package.json`/lockfile, `.gitignore`/`.gitleaks.toml`, anything under the root `scripts/` (it holds the pin tags every workspace resolves from), a `spec/` workspace path (home has none today, dead code as of this landing, kept and tested for when one exists again), or an unclassified path forces `full`; `frontend/` and `backend/` together forces `full` (crosses packages); a backend change touching a path `frontend/` imports directly (found live via `git grep` for `@maipai/home-backend/src/...`, never a hand-kept list; the match strips a known `.ts`/`.tsx`/`.js`/`.jsx` extension from both sides, so it still fires if a future import ever carries a compiled `.js` extension the source file doesn't) also forces `full`; otherwise the one package's scope, or `docs` if only docs changed. `frontend: typecheck` runs under both `frontend` and `backend` scope (the frontend imports typed backend code); `frontend: a11y` stays in `frontend` scope only (it never runs the backend's own suite, so it isn't the flakiness/slowness this rule exists to route around). The secrets scan and PII wordlist run in every scope, unchanged. `check.sh` prints the scope and why as its first line (`== scope: frontend (only frontend/ changed)`); a `--docs` call that turns out wider than docs runs the wider scope and says so rather than silently under-checking; `--full` always forces everything. 19 unit tests in `scripts/gateScope.test.ts` cover every rule (frontend-only, backend-only, docs-only, a bundled package's own README counting as backend not docs, `docs/api/` as backend, `.claude/` as docs, crosses-packages, a root pin/lockfile/scripts/spec/ change, a rename across packages via `--no-renames`, the direct-import escalation both ways and across a `.js`/`.ts` extension mismatch, an empty diff, an untracked file, an unclassified path). A medium review (this touches the gate's own guard logic) found and fixed five real gaps before landing: an "unbound variable" crash under `set -euo pipefail` on an empty changed-file list on this machine's own bash 3.2 (`"${files[@]}"` on a genuinely empty array, a known pre-4.4 bash quirk - the exact "clean tree, nothing to scope" case the empty-diff rule above exists for), a leaked temp-file pair on any failure path (a `RETURN` trap doesn't fire when `set -e` aborts the whole script from inside the function - confirmed live; fixed with an `EXIT` trap whose command string is expanded at registration time, since the function's own locals won't exist by the time a later `EXIT` fires), a stale comment naming a `frontend_imported_backend_paths()` function that was inlined and never actually created under that name, the `.js`-extension gap above, and the missing `spec/` test/doc coverage above. Exit: `bash scripts/check.sh` (its own new scope line, plus a full run to verify the change itself) and the unit tests. **Follow-up, same day (coordinator-directed):** an untracked file left by another session in a shared checkout was still being gathered (`git ls-files --others`) and could widen a run past what `--docs` or the real tracked diff actually needed (live case: a stray `backend/scripts/bench/query-rewrite.ts` widened a `--docs` run to `backend`, four minutes for a docs-only change). Fixed: tracked, changed files decide the scope whenever any exist; untracked files are only consulted as a fallback when nothing tracked changed at all (a review caught a first, naive "drop untracked entirely" fix regressing the ordinary new-file-before-`git add` case back to forcing `full`). New `scripts/checkScope.test.ts` (3 cases) proves the real bash against a real scratch git repo, extracted live from `check.sh` itself, not just `classifyScope()` in isolation. Writing it also hit and fixed `getmaipai/home#144` (a `git grep` "no matches" exit killing the pipeline under `set -e`, dormant on the real repo, immediate on the test's own minimal fixture). See `docs/dev.md`'s own "GATE-SCOPE-01 follow-up" entry for the full record.

<a id="route-find-04"></a>

- [x] **ROUTE-FIND-04: literal routing prefers the most specific pattern, and a discourse "look," is not a command** (S, corpus first, 2026-09-22; from ROUTE-FIND-03 (b)'s review, 2e67fd9e). (a) `routeLiteral()` (`turnEngine.ts` near :1445) resolves two packages' matching patterns by the alphabetical package order of `loadAllManifests()`, not by specificity, so a package sorting after `websearch` with its own "search"/"look up"/"google" pattern is silently shadowed; the music/websearch collision is pinned by a corpus row, the mechanism is not fixed. Fix: among matching patterns, the one with the longest literal prefix wins, ties by package id. (b) `commandOpenersFrom()` takes a pattern's first word as a bare command opener, so "look up *" made "Look, I really think we should talk about this" a directive the memory judge skips; the same trait already misfires on "Put simply, ..." and "Open your eyes to ...". Fix: an opener is the pattern's full literal prefix before the first wildcard, and a first word followed by a comma is never an opener. Tests in these exact words: "look up the artist Adele" routes to music whatever the package order; "Look, I really think we should talk about this" and "Put simply, it's complicated" are not directives. Out of scope: (c) the review's note that "search the house for the keys" routes to websearch, which is the owner's stated rule for a leading "search" (ROUTE-FIND-03 (b)). Exit: `scripts/check.sh` plus the routing corpus replay. **Landed 2026-09-29 (Codex, `254ca1d1`):** both fixes in, the three named tests pass, routing corpus replay 111/111.

<a id="temp-chat-01"></a>

- [x] **TEMP-CHAT-01: a temporary chat that is never remembered** (M, backend first). ChatGPT's temporary chat, and on a household hub whose whole premise is that it remembers, it matters more than it does there: a parent must be able to ask something without it entering history, the thread list, or memory. Not a UI feature - a turn-pipeline one. A conversation marked temporary writes no `conversations` row and no `conversation_turns` rows, and the memory judge never runs on its turns (`backend/src/lib/` memory extraction path); it is gone when the tab closes. **Safety is never skipped**: the safety-first order in `turnEngine.ts`, the role floors and the guards all run exactly as they do on a normal turn (`.github/docs/SAFETY.md`: child-safety protections are non-removable architecture, not a setting), and a child's temporary chat is still age-gated and still subject to every content ceiling. What a temporary chat skips is persistence and memory, nothing else. **Amended 2026-09-22 after Session B found a temporary chat already ships** (Chat 55, `d892052a`, wired into the OLD hand-built chat): turns are already skipped, the thread list already excludes it, minors already get a 403, and the memory judge already cannot see it - but it still writes a content-free `conversations` row. That row goes. What it leaks is metadata (this person had a conversation, on this surface, at this time), which on a household hub is the thing the feature exists to prevent; content-free is not the same as absent. So: no table touched at all, and the multi-turn window lives in process, keyed, size-capped and idle-expired, extending `resumeSessions`/`inFlightTurns` rather than a second store (Session B's catch: a strict zero-row reading without this makes every turn amnesiac, which is a broken chat, not a privacy feature). One implementation, not two - the old chat's call site uses the new path; SHELL-09 deletes the old chat itself. Reasoning: `.github/docs/DECISIONS.md`, 2026-09-22. Entry point: the conversation header's menu (CHAT-HEADER-01) and a New Thread variant, both labelled so a parent understands what is and is not kept. **Widened 2026-09-22, an independent review**: the durable-write audit missed `queueOpenQuestion` (`turnEngine.ts`'s `resolvePendingAsk`, the "who"/"relay" continuation) - unreachable for a temporary conversation in practice (its own `getPendingAsk`/`setPendingAsk` gate already closes the path, proven by a direct test rather than assumed), but named in the acceptance anyway so the guarantee is stated, not inferred from a chain of other things happening to hold. Acceptance: a temporary turn leaves no row in `conversations`, `conversation_turns`, `reply_constraints`, or `open_questions` (asserted directly against the db), the memory judge is never invoked (asserted with a spy), `host.artifact.create()` refuses cleanly instead of hitting the provisional-turn foreign key, the thread list does not show it, a child's temporary turn still hits the same safety path as a normal one (a test that a blocked utterance is still blocked), and reloading loses it. Out of scope: exporting one before it is discarded. Exit: `bash scripts/check.sh`.

- [x] **CHAT-FIND-0923-06: the new-chat composer shifted down on the first keystroke** (S) - **landed 2026-09-23.** A sixth live finding, found separately the same night: typing the first character into a brand-new chat visibly dropped the composer (and the "How can I help you today?" heading above it) down a few pixels. Root cause, in the shared assistant-ui Element (`elements/thread.aui.tsx`): the new-chat welcome block (heading, message group, footer) is vertically centered (`justify-center`) while the chat is empty, and the footer's suggestions row used to unmount entirely the instant the composer stopped being empty (its `AuiIf` gate was `isNewChatView(s) && s.composer.isEmpty`, not just `isNewChatView`). `ViewportFooter` lays its children out with `gap-4`, so unmounting the row removed both its own content height and the one `gap-4` unit before it, shrinking the footer; a shorter centered block re-centers, dropping every element in it - including the heading and composer well above the row that actually changed - by half of whatever height disappeared. Even with zero suggestion chips configured for this household (the row's own content is 0px), the vanishing gap-4 alone is 16px, so the whole block dropped 8px on the very first keystroke; a household with real suggestion chips configured would drop further still. Fixed by keeping the row mounted for the whole new-chat view and toggling only its own visibility (`invisible`, not unmounted) once the composer has text, so the footer's height - and the gap before this row - never changes; a `key`-based remount of just the inner suggestions list still replays its entrance animation each time the composer clears back to empty, matching the pre-fix behavior. Landed in commons first (`ui-v0.5.48`, reviewed low, one round of review findings fixed: a household-fact/quote comment rewritten generically, an unverifiable cross-repo function-name claim removed, the visibility selector hoisted to a named module-level const matching the file's own `isNewChatView` convention, the animation-replay gap closed, and a `dashboard-upstream.md` patch-table row added), then home's own pin bump (reviewed low, zero findings). Acceptance met with a real headless check (`scripts/screenshot.ts --chat-find-composer-shift-review`, new): real `getBoundingClientRect().top` on the composer's own textbox at rest, a 300ms no-keystroke control to rule out a settle-timing artifact (confirmed identical, ruling that out), then after typing one character - 0px delta, confirmed. `bash scripts/check.sh` hit the same shared-machine backend-suite flakiness CHAT-FIND-0923-04 already named as an environment finding that night; frontend build/test/typecheck/eslint/a11y and the standards core all ran directly and passed clean. <a id="handsfree-01"></a>

- [x] **HANDSFREE-01: hands-free, three separate things with three homes** (M). The owner drew the distinction that fixes this row (2026-09-22): the waveform is not the wake word, and neither of them is 'just speak to me'. They differ on two independent axes, how a turn STARTS and how the reply COMES BACK, which gives three features, not one control: **(a) Read replies aloud** - typed turn, spoken reply, no microphone involved. An output setting, so it does NOT live under a voice button; it is a per-conversation setting in the conversation header's menu (CHAT-HEADER-01) beside temporary chat, remembered per person with the conversation (PERSIST-CONV-01). The shipped `read-aloud.tsx` Element does the speaking and also gives the per-message control, which belongs in the message action bar slice 5(e) already built; the toggle only makes it automatic. **(b) Voice conversation** - spoken turn, spoken reply, a mode entered deliberately from the composer's waveform button. **Landed** (found live 2026-09-27, doc catching up to reality): `ComposerExtraEnd` exists on `ThreadComponents` and is wired to `ComposerVoiceControls` in `ChatPage.tsx`; `LiveVoiceSession` runs a real `WS /api/stt/stream` connection, not a stub. This row's own "not mounted" text was stale. **(c) Wake word** - the same mode entered by touching nothing. This is hub-and-device state, not conversation state: if the hub is listening it listens whatever conversation is on screen, so per the one-definition rule it is declared once in the settings registry (`.github/docs/SETTINGS.md`, the generic renderer) and shown on the hub's voice settings page, sourced from an installed wakeword package (catalog `wakewords/`). The composer's chevron may offer a shortcut that flips that same setting; it never owns a second copy of it. **Wake-word invariants (owner's ruling, 2026-09-22, non-negotiable):** a wake word is never always on, the person is always in control, and the person always knows when it is listening. Concretely: (i) **off by default** and it stays off - installing a wakeword package does not enable it, an update never enables it, and no migration or default-restore may turn it on; (ii) **an explicit per-device opt-in** by an adult, one device at a time, never household-wide in one click, and a child profile can never enable it; (iii) **a persistent, unmissable indicator whenever the microphone is open** - visible on the screen the whole time it is listening, not a toast that fades, so a person walking into the room can tell; (iv) **turning it off is always one action** from that indicator itself, never a trip into settings; (v) **nothing before the wake word is kept** - the rolling buffer the detector needs is in memory, never written to disk, never a turn, never a memory record, and the detector runs locally like everything else (PRIVACY.md: nothing leaves the house); (vi) the indicator and the off switch are themselves part of the feature's definition of done, so a build that listens without showing it is a defect, not a missing polish item. Acceptance for these specifically: a fresh install with a wakeword package present listens to nothing (asserted); a child profile cannot reach the toggle (asserted); the indicator is present in the capture whenever the listening state is on and absent when off; and a test proves no pre-wake audio reaches disk, the turn log or the memory judge. Every piece hides when its role or package is unavailable (tts for (a), stt+tts for (b), an installed wake word for (c)), so an unconfigured hub shows none of it. Acceptance: with tts available a typed turn is spoken end to end and the Element's own controls work mid-speech, and the toggle survives a reload of the same conversation; the voice mode is unreachable without stt; the wake-word setting is absent with no wakeword package installed, and toggling it from the composer and from the settings page moves the one same value (asserted, not assumed); a child's turn speaks only content that passed the same safety path. Out of scope: barge-in (talking over a spoken reply to interrupt it), which needs the robot's echo cancellation and gets its own row. Exit: `bash scripts/check.sh` and the captures.

**HANDSFREE-01(a), persisted 2026-09-27 (PERSIST-CONV-01):** the conversation-header read-aloud toggle is stored with that conversation and restored when it is reopened. It remains hidden when TTS is unavailable.
**HANDSFREE-01(c), landed 2026-09-27 (`512da6fb`):** Home adds a default-off, device-scoped wake-word setting, local detector control, a persistent listening indicator with a one-action stop, and the same setting in the composer and Settings. The backend and frontend safety tests cover all six invariants; in particular, a child receives 403 on both device-setting read and write, with no database rows written. Availability currently follows the pinned stock wake-word assets; catalog-based installation remains the separate `WAKEWORD-CATALOG-01` item.

    determiner ("that Answer was wrong"), and a typo one edit from a
    predicate word in a predicate's slot ("Wong, that's not it");
    the tagger's lexicon is the word list, nothing on the network.
    Rule 2: a brand or a service (the tagger's organization tag, a
    model number or a product noun after the name) is unresolved with
    `candidate_kinds: [organization]`, no frame, no ask. Rule 3: a
    name the hub introduced (its last two replies, a retained
    outcome's result text; a name the person said first stays theirs)
    is a `world` subject with that provenance, never unresolved,
    never asked back (`KnownNames.hubNames`, `namesIn()`). Rule 4:
    the `who` answer parser reads the world kinds ("the actress,
    Serena Vale", "a public figure", "she's famous", a full name to a
    first-name ask) into `WhoAnswer.world`; the answer creates no
    entity, retires a candidate of the name, puts a `world` subject of
    that kind on the turn, and runs the turn that raised the name
    (`PendingAsk.carriedQuestion`) as a websearch `via: forced` with
    the engine's query (`worldAnswerQuery()`), so the reply is the
    answer; the model's own identity question about a bare unresolved
    name ("someone you know or a public figure?") binds as the ask
    (`replyAsksIdentityOf()`). The `[turn]` line's subjects carry the
    world kind or the hinted kinds. Bench: not-a-name, hub-named-it,
    public-figure (the fake search's film cast row names Serena Vale),
    `subjectsAbsent` and a subject `kind` as expectation kinds. Tests:
    `backend/tests/ask02.test.ts`. Exit: `bash scripts/check.sh`. The
    full set on bc738b5 (86 rows, three runs): 240, 237, 239 of 302,
    the hard rows 12 of 12, the question rate 27.6 to 29.2 percent;
    LOOKUP-02 and ASK-02 accepted on it. The follow-up commit: the
    lookup stand-down reads the turn's household subjects (things,
    places, the carried ones), the stack deduped by entity; the query
    for a pronoun-only question with no world subject is the

### Model vetting (owner, 2026-10-07)

DONE: Commit 9e951eeb 2026-10-12 "CHAT-LATE-SYSTEM-01: notes ride on their turn" and backend/src/lib/systemFold.ts exists.

- [x] **CHAT-LATE-SYSTEM-01: no system message after the first one reaches the engine** (S, live bug 2026-10-12; architect APPROVED). The Qwen3.5 chat template raises "System message must be at the beginning" (HTTP 500 before streaming), and the history window renders notes about earlier turns (a search stub, a guarded reply, a package or command answer, an unreadable picture) as system-role messages between turns, so any adult turn whose window held one showed "Something went wrong while writing that". Fix, at the source and at the boundary. Source (`conversationHistory.ts`, `nodes/model.ts`): a note about a turn rides on that turn, never as a system message. A guarded or non-model turn's note is attached to the person's message of that turn under the label "Note for you, not written by the person:" (nobody's voice, item 1b; consecutive user messages are accepted by the template, checked on the Stack); an older search stays as the engine's native tool call plus a tool result with the results cleared (`{"results_cleared":true,"source_count":N}`; the newest two turns still replay titles and links); the unreadable-picture note rides on the message the pictures were on. Boundary safety net (`backend/src/lib/systemFold.ts`, in `chatRequestBody()` and `tokenCount.ts`): leading system messages merge into one, any later one is folded verbatim into the adjacent user message and logged once per process, so no new producer can bring the 500 back; counts are taken on what is sent, and a count-only list with no user message is counted net of an empty one (the "No user query found" error). Tests: `backend/tests/systemFold.test.ts`, the updated window tests, and two live smoke turns (`adult-search-asked`, `adult-search-after`). A Stack-side template check (a late system message must be accepted or the model is not vetted) belongs to MODEL-VET-01 check 1.

Live repro (Fable chat test A2): a teen asking "how do I make a classic gin and tonic?" got "That took me too long. Try asking again." twice at 20.1 s. Cause: a minor keeps a wall-clock model deadline (rule 5) and the record's figure (20 s on a model with no Muse record) does not cover a model whose template reasons on every turn (`thinking_mode: "always"`, Muse Glimmer 30B) with the reasoning dropped for a minor. Measured on the Studio's live Stack (read-only, sequential, 8 teen-style safety-shaped prompts, reasoning on, machine under load 20+): first visible text 4.1, 4.2, 5.9, 8.4, 11.7, 13.2, 14.5 s warm and 31.8 s cold (a model swap); about 11 s more for a minor-sized reply; so warm p95 about 26 to 30 s and cold about 43 s. Fix: `resolveTurnBudgetAndEngineModel()` (`backend/src/lib/turnMachine/budget.ts`) raises a child's and a teen's `deadlines_ms.model` to 60 s and `.total` to 90 s (`MINOR_ALWAYS_THINKING_DEADLINES_MS`) when the engine that actually runs has `thinking_mode` "always"; an adult (written replies are uncapped; spoken keep the record) and models that can switch thinking off are unchanged, and no catalog record is mutated. Test `tests/turnMachine/minorAlwaysDeadline.test.ts`. Lands after the v0.2.5 tag.

Two causes, both in the weather package: (1) `manifest.json` `args.properties.place` lacks `"grounded": "conversation"`, so the place the hub's own reply named ("in Chicago" from the household home) is refused as `ungrounded_args` by the policy node and the fixed honesty line replaces the answer (the show_images `subject` seam already does this); (2) `recipe.json`'s format step binds the daily forecast only under `block_*` keys, which `withoutBlockOnlyData()` strips before the model sees the result, so the model truthfully says the data covers only today. Fix: the `grounded` flag, and the daily arrays again under model-visible names (`forecast_dates`, `forecast_highs`, `forecast_lows`, `forecast_rain_chance`); the patch and three policy tests are in the Fable chat-test notes (`weather-catalog-fix.patch`, verified green against `backend/tests/turnMachine/policy.test.ts`, `weatherCard.test.ts`, `smoke.test.ts`). Cause to confirm: the retry round's model output had no text and nothing in `answer.ts`'s `model_text` case guards an empty text (the `from_outcomes` case does, with `COMPOSE_FAILURE_LINE`). Fix: an empty text after a missed lookup becomes the model's own note on a second try with a larger ceiling, or failing that the shared technical-failure line, never silence. Regression test first. The fixed line is a last resort only when the model wrote no words; rule 6 forbids fixed wording otherwise, so the owner may want to rule on it. Tests in `toolRecovery.test.ts`.

A rerun without the picture call answered fully. Tests in `refusedCallKeepsText.test.ts`.

The assistant-ui streaming-text Element renders one plain paragraph with no markdown, so it cannot be the reply renderer; its look (each word fades in blue over 500 ms and settles to ink over 700 ms, a pulsing blue caret after the last word) is drawn by CSS transitions in the kit's `markdown-text.css` on Streamdown's own word spans and `caret` prop inside `MarkdownText`, with the Element left untouched (a Streamdown keyframe was tried first in ui-v0.5.111 and measured cut to under 20 ms, because Streamdown restamps shown words with a 0 ms duration). - [x] **MDNS-HOST-01: starting Home must never rename the computer** (S, 2026-10-04, URGENT; owner-reported). Cause (verified in `bonjour-service` `dist/lib/service.js`): `publish()` in `backend/src/lib/mdns.ts` passed no `host`, so the library defaulted it to `os.hostname()` and announced the machine's OWN `.local` name (SRV target, A and AAAA records); macOS's mDNSResponder saw a conflicting claim on its own host name and renamed the computer ("... (2)", "-2"), and a scratch Home started by `smoke:chat` made it worse. Fix: the service publishes under `maipai-<first 8 of the instance id>.local`, so no record names the machine; `MAIPAI_MDNS=off` (also the default under `NODE_ENV=test` and for any Home that sets the one-hub opt-out) publishes nothing, and `smoke:chat`, `screenshot.ts` and `restore-drill.ts` set it; turning it off clears a stale advertise_failed warning; one log line names the host label. Verified-at 2026-10-04: `backend/tests/mdns.test.ts`. Local check still to run by the owner after the next hub start: `scutil --get ComputerName` and `scutil --get LocalHostName` unchanged, and `dns-sd -G v4 maipai-<id>.local` resolves to this machine. Exit check: `backend/tests/mdns.test.ts`, `scripts/check.sh`.
  Status: verified at 3414c637.

Bar 1 and the VOICE-LIVE-02 proxy pass cleanly under every condition; Bar 2 (tool_call within 2.5s) passes under realistic warm-household usage and is an accepted exception on a fully cold first turn (a pre-existing interim-rule prefill cost, not a regression this item introduces - follow-up named for whoever owns that round's own prefix-cache economics next); Bar 3's own estimate is inconclusive rather than failing under the same cold condition. A medium review and two follow-up verification passes found and fixed real bugs (both in the shipped code and in the bench script itself) before this ticked - full account in dev.md's own "STREAM-NEXT-01" sections.** Objective: `runTurnNext()` always awaited the whole machine to "done" before returning anything, so `/stream` on the new path sent one batched blob (turn_meta, signal, tool events, done) exactly like the immediate route - the same defect LIVE-0923-01 and READ-PAGE-01's own live conversation felt as a long silence before anything appeared. Design collision found and ruled on before any code: `nodes/outputGate.ts`'s `output_gate` node already runs a whole-reply `evaluateReply()` on every new-path turn, a second safety mechanism the old path has no equivalent of; getmaipai-26's ruling resolves it as "one node, one floor function, two granularities, one authority" (full ruling quoted in dev.md) rather than either bypassing output_gate or letting it retroactively override an already-streamed reply. Built exactly to that ruling: `outputGate.ts` exports `StreamGate`, a push-driven per-sentence gate (the identical `evaluateSafety()`/`forOutput()` floor `evaluateReply()` already uses, `nextSentenceBoundary()` from the spec's own chunker) that `nodes/model.ts`'s `runOneGeneration()` feeds raw deltas into for any non-forced generation (`tool_choice !== "required"`, point 6), think-split live first so reasoning never streams (point 5); a generation whose first non-space character is `{` or `<` is held whole, never released (point 4, the envelope guard - broadened from `{` alone by a follow-up review pass, since the tag-wrapped form is the actual live miss, ENGINE-CONTRACT-03); the chunker's own final tail alone is repaired against the whole delivered reply (`repairTail`, point 3, matched to `turnEngine.ts`'s own `gateOutputSafety()` after a review caught the isolated-tail version misdiagnosing a quote opened in an earlier sentence) before release. `output_gate`'s own node reads the gate's already-made verdict back (`state.streamGate?.result()`) instead of re-evaluating a streamed reply's text, so the logged turn is exactly the concatenation of what was released, by construction (point 1) - unchanged for every other AnswerInput kind and every immediate-path turn (the gate is never populated). A refusal (`push()`/`finish()` never throw - nothing above them in the machine's own async call chain is built to catch a mid-node throw) closes the delivery queue immediately via `onRefuse`, so `runTurnNextStream()`'s own `tokens` generator throws `StreamSafetyRefusal` (the identical class and wire behavior `turnEngine.ts`'s old path already uses) without waiting for the rest of that generation or the machine to finish; `finalize()` mirrors this, building and logging the fixed refusal line synchronously from `state` (settled long before generation starts) the instant the wire needs it, rather than racing a background promise it can't await (point 2). A live tool_call/tool_result never existed on the wire for streaming on either path - `nodes/tool.ts` pushes the identical "On it." status line the old path already emits before a tool runs, onto the same `StatusChannel` (`state.status`, set only by `runTurnNextStream()`), so it reaches a live client before the search itself finishes. `routes/turn.ts`'s own `ResumeSession`/`streamResponse`/`streamTurnEvents()` machinery needed no change at all: it already branches on `TurnStreamResult`'s own `kind`, generically, for any producer - only its `/stream` route's own dispatch (`newPathOn()` now calls `runTurnNextStream()`, not `runTurnNext()`) changed, one line. Files: `turnMachine/contract.ts` (`TurnState.status`/`streamGate`, both optional), `turnMachine/nodes/outputGate.ts` (`StreamGate`, the node's new streamed branch), `turnMachine/nodes/model.ts` (`runOneGeneration`'s gate wiring, think-split), `turnMachine/nodes/tool.ts` (the live status line), `turnMachine/turnNext.ts` (`beginTurn`/`finishTurn` split, `runTurnNextStream`, a `drainDeltaQueue()` generator over a `StatusChannel<string>` - `StatusChannel` made generic by a follow-up review pass rather than a second, hand-rolled queue), `routes/turn.ts` (the `/stream` route's own dispatch), `tests/turnMachine/outputGate.test.ts` (18 direct `StreamGate` unit tests, two added by follow-up review passes: the tag-wrapped envelope, a quote spanning a sentence boundary), `tests/turnMachine/turnNext.test.ts` (eight end-to-end tests against the real streaming stub server: logged-equals-streamed, adult and child mid-stream refusal, finalize-never-waits, the live tool status line, a retry-preserves-the-gate regression, a non-refuse crisis-resources regression, the existing immediate-path test unchanged). `bash scripts/check.sh` green (backend scope; full suite 4174/4174, no regression). One commit, not two: commits (a) and (b) share the same `StatusChannel`/`StreamGate` wiring end to end (a "stream" kind result needs `state.streamGate` to be anything but an inert batch anyway), and there is no independently meaningful stopping point between them - flagged to the coordinator rather than forced apart. Out of scope, named rather than silently worked around: an engine-crash-mid-generation's own logged text can diverge from what streamed (the machine's existing `model_failed` fallback is unchanged, a pre-existing risk class, not a new one); a household's own `bannedPhrases` filler-repeat guard (turnEngine.ts's `bannedPhrasesFor()`) has no new-path equivalent yet, so a streamed thinking cue can repeat a phrase an old-path turn already used - cosmetic only. Tests in these words (all landed): a streamed turn's logged reply equals the concatenation of the released deltas; a sentence the floor refuses mid-stream stops the stream the old path's way, on an adult turn and a child turn; a generation opening with `{` emits no delta; a reply ending in dangling markup is released repaired; the existing output_gate tests pass unchanged on immediate turns. Exit: `bash scripts/check.sh` green; the hold-protocol live bench (new: `scripts/bench/stream-next-01-live.ts`), all bars cleared on two live runs, full numbers in dev.md.

Objective: `conv-19awhetzdf` - all three SearXNG upstream engines suspended, every query answered `results: []`, read as a plain succeeded outcome with nothing to answer from; the phrasing round answered from its own knowledge instead, wrongly, contradicting the person three times. A pre-existing safety floor (`output_gate`'s COMMAND-FAIL-01 provenance check, which unconditionally swaps any failed outcome's `userMessage` for the generic `COMPOSE_FAILURE_LINE`) is worked with, not around: `answer.ts` gains `toolOutageLine(errorCode)`, the identical fixed-code-to-line mapping `policyRefusalLine` already uses, recognizing only `search_unavailable` and delivering it untagged; every other code still gets the generic swap. A genuine "nothing found" (empty rows, no engine errors) stays a real succeeded outcome and still runs the phrasing round, but the websearch package's one `synthesis_hint` (`recipe.json`) is strengthened to explicitly say: if rows is empty, say plainly nothing was found, never answer from your own knowledge, never contradict the person - a model instruction conditioned on data already in the message, never a code-level word rule. Also fixed along the way: `tool.ts`'s own outcome-building carried the numeric HTTP status as `errorCode` instead of the semantic HostError code (`commands.ts`, its sibling, already did this correctly) - without this fix `toolOutageLine` could never have matched anything. **A medium review (per org policy - a guard and a wire shape) found and fixed two real regressions before this landed: `searxngHealth.ts`'s own periodic canary check would have raised the wrong issue (a URL-check message) for tonight's exact incident, since it had no way to tell `search_unavailable` apart from a truly unreachable instance; and the emptiness check itself only looked at `rows`, never `infoboxes`, so a real infobox-only answer (Wikipedia's own shape) alongside some unrelated suspended engine would have been misclassified as a total outage - both fixed, two new regression tests. Three smaller findings fixed (a losable errorCode guarantee widened to match turnEngine.ts's own established pattern, a doubled status check, a cross-reference comment); two accepted and named (a small, deliberate action-array duplication in machine.ts; toolOutageLine's own mapping living in a different file from where its message is authored) - full account in dev.md.** Files: `packageHost.ts`, `searxngHealth.ts`, `turnMachine/machine.ts`, `turnMachine/nodes/tool.ts`, `turnMachine/nodes/answer.ts`, `packages/websearch/recipe.json`, `scripts/bench/conversationRunner.ts`. Objective: the health row, admin notifications on down and on recovery, quiet mode with a 15-minute probe, one token bucket per host with its numbers stated, and a bench runner that refuses a real SearXNG URL without clearance. Change: `packageHost.ts`'s `searxngSearch()` now reports every real outcome (ok, degraded, down) through a new shared leaf module, `searchHealthState.ts`, the moment it happens - `searxngHealth.ts`'s own hourly-turned-15-minute canary calls the identical function, so the two detection paths land on the same two Repairs rows rather than two driftable copies; a self-imposed `rate_limited` throw is excluded from health reporting at both call sites. `issues.ts`'s `resolveIssue()` gains a new, generic `repairs.resolved` notification on the exact symmetric transition `raiseIssue()`'s own `repairs.new` already fires on - every existing error-severity issue source gets a recovery notification for free, nothing bespoke to search. The scheduler's own canary cadence tightened from `every:1h` to `every:15m`, unconditionally (a single request every 15 minutes is nowhere near the tightened rate budget below, and it means an outage or its recovery is caught in minutes either way, not only while already known to be down). The already-existing shared SearXNG rate limiter's numbers tightened from `{capacity: 10, refillPerSecond: 0.5}` to the design note's own stated budget, `{capacity: 3, refillPerSecond: 1/6}` (a burst of three, then about one every six seconds) - tonight's own 25-query bench run fit comfortably inside the old numbers, which is exactly how it went unnoticed as flooding. **A design question resolved rather than asked: "waits for a person's turn" is not a queuing mechanism to build - the shared rate limiter's own contract is deliberately "never blocks or queues," a foundational choice this item has no business weakening for one caller; a rejected call's existing honest refusal already means the person just tries again.** `scripts/bench/liveHubQuiet.ts` gains `refuseRealSearxngWithoutClearance()`, refusing a real (non-`127.0.0.1`/`localhost`) SearXNG URL unless `MAIPAI_BENCH_REAL_SEARXNG_CLEARED=1` is set per invocation; `query-writer-01-live.ts` (whose own 2026-09-24 run sent the 25 real queries) is retrofitted to call it. **A medium review (a guard, per instruction) found and fixed four real bugs: the health-reporting try/catch originally wrapped the `read_page` fetch too, misreporting a failed linked page as SearXNG being down; the tightened rate limit was still shared with page reads, so one question with `read_page: true` cost two tokens from one bucket, a real risk to ordinary conversation the review's own third angle asked about directly - fixed with a separate page-read budget; `resolveIssue()`'s new notification wasn't wrapped in `trackBackgroundWork()`, reproducing the exact class of bug getmaipai/home#123 fixed that mechanism for; the canary's own catch redundantly re-recorded a "down" outcome `searxngSearch()` had already recorded. Full account in dev.md.** `repairs.resolved` is `configurable: false` (in-app only, unlike `repairs.new`'s Telegram toggle) - its own settings key is a shared-spec record (commons's `spec/settings/keys.json`) and the gate's own drift check refused a first cut that added it without bumping that pin, out of scope for this item. Files: `searchHealthState.ts` (new), `packageHost.ts`, `searxngHealth.ts`, `issues.ts`, `notificationTypes.ts`, `index.ts`, `liveHubQuiet.ts`, `query-writer-01-live.ts`. Tests (fourteen new/changed): real-call health reporting, the tightened rate limit's own numbers, a failed page read never misreporting SearXNG as down, and the split search/page-read budgets (`packageHost.test.ts`); `repairs.resolved` firing once on a genuine transition, never for warning/info or while dismissed (`issues.test.ts`); the URL classification the bench refusal depends on (`liveHubQuiet.test.ts`). Out of scope: a background search caller (none exists yet, so "nothing in the background" needed no new gate); SEARCH-FALLBACK-01, next in the queue. **Follow-up, same day, dev.md "SEARCH-HEALTH-01 follow-up": the bench guard moved to `setup.ts` itself (the real choke point every live bench passes through, not just the one script it was first wired into); the 15-minute probe now applies only while search is down or degraded, an hourly no-op tick otherwise (the first cut's unconditional 96-request-a-day cadence was exactly the fan-out THIRD-PARTY-SERVICES.md rules out). A low review on that same fix-up found two more real bugs: the throttle's own health check excluded dismissed-but-still-broken issues (silently falling back to hourly while dismissed); the bench guard's URL classifier failed open on an unparseable value instead of refusing it. Both fixed, seven new tests total.** **B-GUARD-02, follow-up, an independent review of SEARCH-HEALTH-01/SEARCH-PACE-01/SEARCH-FALLBACK-01 together (2026-09-24, dev.md "B-GUARD-02"): the bench guard existed as two independently-maintained copies (setup.ts's own inline check, keyed to one env var name, and liveHubQuiet.ts's `refuseRealSearxngWithoutClearance()`) - `stream-next-01-live.ts` read a THIRD, differently-named env var neither copy ever saw, so every run of it reached the household's real SearXNG with zero clearance gate. Fixed: setup.ts's own copy deleted outright; every real caller (`query-writer-01-live.ts`, already correct; `interimRuleMeasure.ts`; `stream-next-01-live.ts`, renamed to the shared env var name) now calls the one surviving definition directly, at its own point of writing `search.searxng_url`. Ten new tests (three unit-level on the shared function via a real spawned process, three end-to-end on stream-next-01-live.ts's own real wiring, plus the four pre-existing ones this cleanup left untouched); five obsolete tests exercising the deleted setup.ts copy removed. Full backend suite green (4221/4221); low review.** Exit: `bash scripts/check.sh`; the fourteen plus seven tests, landed.

      used - so the privacy promise itself has likely never held.

      `INCOGNITO-11` below. Exit: `bash scripts/check.sh` (both slices

No separate child-view rule was needed: `canAccessFile` already governs a shared file's visibility independent of the viewer's role, so the design record's own "not a new rule invented for profiles, it's STORE-SHARE-01's own disclosure filter read from a second surface" held exactly as written. **A real gap surfaced building this**: nothing anywhere in this codebase served a file's own bytes over HTTP before now (checked directly - only `lib/attachments.ts`'s `readAttachment` existed, called from `documentExtraction.ts` and tests, never a route), so `MediaGrid`'s `thumbnailUrl` had nowhere real to point; - [x] **STORE-DELETE-01: a deleted person's files** (S, Sonnet; after STORE-SPEC-01). Objective: the existing person-deletion path (`backend/src/lib/personLifecycle.ts`) gains one step in one place: the person's files with no live share pointer are purged with the person, records and blobs (a blob only when no record points at it); a file with any live share remains, its ownership passes to the household, it counts against the household cap and no personal cap, and the person's name stays in provenance. Mirror: the memory store's tombstones on person deletion. Acceptance, in these exact words: bramble creates a picture and shares it with lucia, lucia shares it with the family, bramble's account is deleted: the picture remains, listed under the household, counted against the household cap, with bramble in its provenance; a second picture bramble never shared is gone, blob and record, after an export was offered; a memorialized person's files all remain (decision 5). Exit: `bash scripts/check.sh`. **Done 2026-10-06:** the one step is `releaseFilesOfDeletedPerson()` in the new `backend/src/lib/storage/personFiles.ts`, called once from `erasePersonData()` before the turns are erased. Pointers addressed to the person are removed and any re-share they made from someone else's pointer is pruned (`pruneUnreachableShares` gained a `departingPersonId`, since the tombstone is written after erasure); then each file they own either has a live share and stays (conversation and turn cleared, retention `kept`, new hlc) or is purged by the new `purgeFileRecord()` (pointers and record; the blob is unlinked by `deletePerson()` only after its transaction commits, so a rollback never leaves a record without bytes). A pointer counts as live only when it reaches the household or a living person, so a stale pointer to someone deleted earlier keeps nothing; a same-bytes pointer counts, since the other person's upload is that record. The confirmation's Remove button waits for the preview, so the export is always offered first. A file an earlier departed person left to the household is purged when the last person it was shared with is deleted. "Passes to the household" is derived from the owner's tombstone, not written: `file.schema.json` says `owner_person_id` is "always a person, never the household" and captured at write time, so the record keeps the deleted person as owner, which is their place in its provenance. `householdUsageBytes()` already sums every record and personal caps apply only to the writer, so the file counts against the household cap and nobody's personal cap; `storageUsageOverview()` adds `household.inherited` (the Storage page's "Shared by people no longer here" row) and the Library lists such a file as "Household, shared by <name>" (`household`, `former_owner_name` on `GET /api/files`, additive). The export: no export existed in the deletion path, so `GET /api/people/{id}/deletion-preview` tells the delete confirmation how many files go and stay, and `GET /api/people/{id}/files/export` streams a gzip tar (bytes plus `files.json` of File records, through the `tar` package from a scratch folder of hard links beside the attachments folder, so nothing large is held in memory or copied, and a cancelled download stops the packer and removes the folder) under the memory export's rule: yourself, or a parent for a child; a teen's or adult's private files are never handed to the admin removing them, the confirmation tells them to ask the person instead. Memorialization never calls the step, so every file stays. Migration 0088 rebuilds `attachments` with nullable `conversation_id`/`turn_id`; drizzle-kit's generated SQL failed on a database with share pointers (drizzle runs migrations in one transaction, where `PRAGMA foreign_keys=OFF` is a no-op), so the pointers are copied aside and restored around the rebuild, with a test migrating a seeded pre-0088 database. Also fixed on the way: the old delete path and `host.data.forget` both threw a foreign-key error for a person with any shared file, and a temporary chat's in-memory pictures now go with the person. Tests: `backend/tests/storeDelete.test.ts` (the acceptance in its filed words, the child export, memorialization, pointer pruning, the last-recipient purge, forget, the migration), `backend/tests/personDeletionChatPictures.test.ts` (two pictures through the upload route, one sent and one in an unsent message, deleted with the person, a directory sweep proving only the shared picture is left), and frontend tests for the confirmation, the Library label and the Storage row.

Two blocking backend gaps found, both required before polling shows anything real: (1) `runner.ts` only saves project state once per finished BATCH, not per step - `bedtime-storybook`'s three chapters run as one parallel batch, so a poll today sees "all pending" then "all three done" with nothing in between; add a read-only `liveProject(id)` returning the running in-memory object `steps.ts` already mutates per-step, and have the GET route prefer it while the project is live. (2) the frontend never learns the project's id at all - `wire.ts`'s `TurnValue` has no `project` field (mirror the existing `artifact?` field at line ~268); add it live from the `start_project` tool outcome and on reload via a new `projectsByTurn()` lookup (mirror `artifactsByTurn()`, keyed on `provenance.turnId`, no new column). v1 progress granularity is a step counter/status line ("Writing chapter-2 (2 of 3)") built from each `StepState`'s `stepId`/`state` - no percentages or token streaming exist in the runner today, and streaming raw generated text is explicitly out (SAFETY.md: a text artifact is gated as a whole, never shown unchecked before its safety check runs). Render as the already-shipped `JobProgress` kit element (`commons/ui/src/elements/job-progress.tsx`) inside a new reserved tool-call part (`project`, mirroring how `write_document`/`tool_timeline`/`sources` already work as reserved standalone tool renders in `ChatPage.tsx`'s `useAssistantToolUI` set) with `refetchInterval` ~2s, stopping on `done`/`failed`/`cancelled`; `onCancel` calls the existing `POST /api/projects/:id/cancel`. On finish, the live tab needs to show the posted artifact without a reload - GET response gains an optional sibling field (e.g. `posted_artifact: {id, version} | null`, looked up by the `project:<id>` tag `post.ts` already writes) so the render can show the `ArtifactCard` itself; hide it once the turn's own reload path would carry the real `artifact` field, to avoid a double card. Do NOT hold assistant-ui's own run open for the project's duration - a self-refreshing tool part is the correct shape, not a blocked composer. Files: `backend/src/lib/projects/runner.ts`, `backend/src/lib/projects/store.ts` (new `projectsByTurn()`), `backend/src/routes/projects.ts`, `backend/src/wire.ts` (`TurnValue.project`), the turn's done-value assembly for `start_project` outcomes (`turnNext.ts`/`composer.ts`), `backend/src/lib/conversationHistory.ts`, `frontend/src/lib/api.ts` (`api.project()`/`api.cancelProject()`), `frontend/src/apps/chat/{chatModelAdapter,chatHistoryAdapter}.ts`, `frontend/src/shell/pages/ChatPage.tsx`. Out of scope, named as follow-ups: PROJECT-PROGRESS-02 (each finished chapter appearing as it completes, needs a route serving one step's own gated text), an optional per-step `label` in the spec for nicer status lines, a real live push transport (only if some future feature needs genuinely sub-second continuity - this item's own poll interval is not that feature). Exit: `bash scripts/check.sh` (medium review - this changes a route shape and the wire) plus a runner test proving a mid-batch poll sees a chapter running or done (not just pending-then-all-done), a history test for the reload lookup, and a frontend render test covering polling, the stop condition, and cancel.

Objective: the existing spec area `home` ("Home settings", `/settings/home`, `min_role: admin`, `commons/spec/settings/areas.json`) becomes the one place for household administration, with a visible entry: the kit's `RailProfileMenu` already takes a `homeSettings` row and Home never passes it (`frontend/src/shell/RailProfile.tsx` line 42 passes only `settingsHref`), so today an admin can reach Home settings only through old `?tab=household` links. Shown only to role owner or admin (and hidden for a minor's band if a minor ever holds one); the hub keeps its own gates (`requireRole`/`requireRoleOrGrant` on engine link, engines, people, backups; household-scope writes refused in `lib/settings.ts` line 83). Personal settings (Account, Chat settings, each app's own lists and voice) stay in the person's own areas and are never drawn in Home settings. Grouping, all as `areas.json` sections drawn by the kit `SettingsShell`: General (household name, home location, locale, status), People (Users, Family links), Engines and AI (AI models, Engines, AI tuning, engine computer pairing, Hugging Face token), Devices (add a robot, robot passwords, robot settings), Search, Integrations, Commands, Voices, Storage and backups, Maintenance (Updates, Repairs, Performance, Status), Privacy, Developer (plugin routing stats). Migration note, today's household-level surfaces and where each lands: Users `/users` (linked, stays), Family `/people` (linked, stays), AI models `/models` and Engines `/engines` (linked, stay until ENGINES-AI-01; superseded: both now redirect to Engines and AI and draw inside it), Backups `/backups`, Storage `/storage`, Updates, Repairs, Performance, Status, Privacy (linked, stay), household keys `household.system`/`status`/`search`/`integrations`/`notifications`/`reference`/`ai`/`storage` (already cards, stay); with no entry today and moving in as `view` sections: engine computer pairing (`apps/settings/EngineLinkCredentialSection.tsx`), add a robot (`AddRobotSection.tsx`), robot password rotation (`RobotPasswordSection.tsx`), Hugging Face token (`HuggingFaceTokenSection.tsx`), plugin routing stats (`RoutingStatsSection.tsx`); each moves port before delete, and the dead old page `apps/settings/SettingsPage.tsx` and `apps/settings/DevicesPage.tsx` are deleted once nothing imports them. Child and teen rule: Home settings holds household scope only. Admins never see anyone's personal places, lists or location, a child's included (owner rule 2026-10-08); the only location in Home settings is `household.home`. Other person-scoped settings keep the 2026-09-30 ruling: reached from People > that person, a child's by an owner or admin, never a teen's or another adult's; nothing here widens it. Person-scoped keys with selector `location` (the weather and maps place lists and defaults) are excluded from People > that person for every role, a child's included (PLACE-HUB-01). Reuse check: the area, the shell, the profile-menu row and every section component already exist; this item wires and moves, it builds no new screen. Acceptance: a test that the menu row shows for owner and admin and not for adult, teen, child or guest; a test that a non-admin opening `/settings/home` lands on Account; a test per moved section that it renders inside Home settings; a test that no person-scope key appears in the `home` area; a test that People > a child's settings, opened as owner or admin, returns no location-selector key or value; captures of the menu and each section at 1440 and 390 in both themes opened and judged. Out of scope: new admin features, any change to `canAccessPerson`, the person's own PIN change (the old `ChangeSecretSection.tsx` is deleted; filed as ACCOUNT-PIN-CHANGE-01). Exit: `commons` check if `areas.json` changes, pin bump, `bash scripts/check.sh`.

Objective: the weather parts carry a condition code, and the card renders an animated icon for it plus a condition background (the old Home's weather app did this well: amCharts' animated SVG weather icons, downloaded at build time by `scripts/fetch-third-party.mjs` with pinned sha256 sums per file and the licence file kept beside them, never tracked; and `WeatherHeroBg.tsx`'s CSS-animated rain, snow and cloud layers over a gradient chosen by condition and time of day; both in `legacy-backups/home-legacy.git`, reference only, the fetch pattern and the effect parameters are the hard-won part). Rule kept: the icon set is a download, pinned and checksummed (the org's third-party rule), rendered as an `<img>` in the Elements' own card slot; the background is tokens and CSS on the card the Element renders, no hand-built component. Applies to the chat's weather card, the dashboard's Today card (DASH-CARDS-01) and the glance surface. Acceptance: every condition the package can emit maps to an icon and a background (a test over the mapping), day and night variants, reduced-motion honoured, the fetch verified against the sums in the gate, captures of three conditions. Exit: `bash scripts/check.sh`.

- [ ] **CONV-ARCHIVE-01: a real archive, shared by both conversation menus** (M, spec first; coordinator's own row, 2026-09-23, not yet picked up). The shipped `elements/thread-list.aui.tsx`'s own three-dots menu always offers Archive (Rename/Archive/Delete, no capability flag to hide one), but `chatThreadListAdapter.ts`'s own `archive()`/`unarchive()` throw unconditionally by deliberate design ("the shared record has no archive state. Do not expose an action that silently deletes a conversation or disappears on reload") - a real, pre-existing gap, not a hand-built limitation to route around. This item closes it: the conversation record gains `archived_at` in `@maipai/spec` (spec first, the shared record shapes go through the spec before either client), the adapter's `archive()`/`unarchive()` set/clear it instead of throwing, an archived conversation leaves the live thread list into the shipped Element's own archived section (it has one - verify before assuming) with an unarchive control, and then both the thread row's own menu and the header's own conversation-actions menu (CHAT-FIND-0923-03) carry a real, working Archive - the header's own item drawn from the one real capability, not a second copy. Acceptance: archiving a conversation from either menu removes it from the live list and shows it in the archived section; unarchiving from there restores it to the live list; a child's own conversations archive/unarchive the same way (no role gate named otherwise); the header's own Archive item does the same real thing the row's own does. Exit: `bash scripts/check.sh` and the captures.

    Status (2026-09-13, a first slice, left open): the baseline

    forty sequences, five repeats, both transports, the thresholds)

    Status (2026-09-13, later): the fixture is 30 conversations (the
    Cobra film set, four other-kind subjects, three household
    subjects, item 1b of `docs/plans/baseline-fixes-2026-09-13.md`;
    a cancel row and a promise row from the effect standard of
    `docs/plans/conversation-competencies-2026-09-13.md`, with ten
    rows rewritten to observe the effect rather than the reply's
    words) and its table is the chat regression suite: every item that
    touches a turn reports its three runs against it. The last series
    on the 28-conversation fixture was 91, 91 and 85 of 98 scored
    turns; the rewritten rows that need unbuilt pieces (the registry
    read into a turn, a reconciled interruption, a lookup with a
    source) fail on purpose until their items land.

    Depends on: CHAT-02 through CHAT-21 and CHAT-22. Files:
    `spec/llm/{routing,tool-call,guard,naturalness}-corpus.json`,
    `backend/scripts/bench/memory/{fixture,run}.ts`, existing bench runners,
    and the corresponding backend/frontend tests. Extend current corpora
    with stable IDs and separate deterministic control-flow fixtures from
    semantic paraphrase live cases. Do not delete paraphrases because the
    bag-of-words stub cannot solve them. At minimum add 40 sequences:
    eight disclosure/search/correction/recall, eight ambiguous/pronoun
    follow-ups, eight no-tool near-matches, eight two-tool/partial-failure/
    confirmation cases, and eight current/historical/privacy cases. Add
    the four report guard probes and credential/output-safety regressions
    to permanent deterministic tests.

    Acceptance: grade retrieval and capture against expected source IDs, scopes,
    validity, and active record counts. For phrasing use a local judge with
    explicit supported/contradicted/missing claims, retaining synthetic
    evidence and a disagreement list; never let its grade override
    deterministic safety/action assertions. Run each live sequence five
    times in both transports. Require zero observed privacy, credential,
    safety-floor, or false-success failures; at least 95% correct routing
    and required-fact answers, at least 98% capture precision, at least
    90% capture recall, and at most 2% false-tool calls. Report Wilson 95%
    intervals, denominators, failures, and unavailable cases. The thresholds
    are acceptance targets, not claims about current accuracy.

    Measure at least 30 warm turns per condition with/without background
    work: p50/p95 first text/audio, total time, cancellation, and memory
    headroom. Require no more than 10% p95 foreground slowdown under
    background load and no more than 10% ordinary-chat first-text regression
    versus the same-build baseline. Failure leaves this item open with
    findings; never weaken the gate. Out of scope: production rollout.
    Checks: relevant deterministic suites, isolated live bench reports,
    seeded browser/audio exercise, and full exit gate.

       live. Add one thinking-mode trial: five hard questions with
       `thinking: true` on each model, total time and whether the
       answer is right.
    4. Record one table in dev.md with both columns side by side, the
       engine build, both model files and checksums, and the machine.

    Verdict rule (from CHAT-24, not softened): the candidate qualifies
    for a promotion recommendation only if it holds every correctness
    floor (zero false tool calls, every positive selected, guard hits
    not higher, no naturalness row worse, register consistency not
    lower for any companion, all four probes answered without a cut,
    all three household negatives still caught) AND either first-delta
    p95 improves by at least 15% or total p50 by at least 20%. Otherwise
    the verdict is "keep the 8B", recorded with the numbers, and the
    question is closed until a new model generation appears. A
    recommendation is not a switch: changing the default chat model, a
    hub deploy, or a download on the hub is the owner's explicit call.
    Out of scope: control vectors (EVAL-03), a draft model (EVAL-02),
    the background engine's model (MEM-05 owns it), any prompt change.
    Checks: the benches' own tests, then the full exit gate for the
    catalog entry.

    <a id="invest-01"></a>

    Depends on: CHAT-15 (typed outcomes), CHAT-16 (native tool-result
    messages and the shared composer), CHAT-17 (the streaming state
    machine), JOIN-01 (episode recall in the prompt), THINK-01 for the
    compose-step thinking gate (may land after, with the gate off).
    Files: `backend/src/lib/turnEngine.ts` and the CHAT-17 machine,
    `turnContext.ts`, `llm.ts`, `spec/llm/ts/types.ts` only if an
    observation field is missing from the tool-result message shape,
    `backend/src/routes/turn.ts` (progress text through the existing
    cue event, additive), `backend/tests/tier2.test.ts`,
    `turnEngine.test.ts`, `spec/llm/tool-call-corpus.json`. Mirror
    CHAT-16's decision table and CHAT-17's phases; add a phase, do not
    add a second machine. Read the dev.md design note first; its limits
    are the constants here, named and tested, changed only with a
    measurement.

    Do, in this order:
    1. Observation shape: from each `ToolExecutionOutcome`, build the
       tool-result message content as `{ source, as_of, status:
       found|missing|error, facts }` where `facts` is the result's
       `data` plus `synthesis_hint`, bounded by CHAT-12's budget. Nothing
       from a result enters a system message.
    2. The loop: after a round executes, if the round contained no
       consequential proposal and the round budget is not spent, run one
       more decision completion with the observations appended as tool
       results and the same pre-filtered read-only tool list (plus
       always-offer). Constants: `INVESTIGATION_MAX_ROUNDS = 2`,
       `INVESTIGATION_MAX_CALLS = 4`, `INVESTIGATION_DEADLINE_MS` of
       12,000 for voice surfaces and 25,000 for `chat`. Calls within a
       round run concurrently as today. A consequential proposal at any
       point ends the loop and goes to the existing confirmation; nothing
       else from that batch executes.
    3. Exhaustion: when any budget is hit, compose from what is
       supported and name what stayed unresolved in one plain sentence.
       Never a third round, never a repeated call.
    4. Progress: when a round's execution passes the cue threshold, the
       cue text is derived from the executing tool's user-facing
       description (FAST-03's sentence), for example "Checking Saturday's
       hours." Reuse the `spoken_cue` event; add no new event type.
    5. Thinking at compose: if THINK-01 exists, enable thinking for the
       compose completion when observations conflict (two facts with the
       same subject and different values) or there are three or more
       observations; otherwise leave it off.
    6. Tests, with scripted tool calls keyed on whether the request
       already carries tool-result messages: the museum scenario (round
       one: episode recall returns last week's constraints, the venue
       tool returns hours plus "Saturday sold out"; the scripted second
       decision asks for Sunday; round two returns it; the composed
       answer names the conflict and recommends Sunday); a budget test
       (a scripted model that keeps asking for more gets exactly two
       rounds and four calls, then an answer that names the unresolved
       part); a consequential test (a "book it" proposal in round two
       produces the confirmation and executes nothing); a control test
       (a greeting takes one completion and zero tool calls, a timer
       takes zero completions); a deadline test using the existing
       timing hooks, no real sleeps. Add the scenario rows to the
       tool-call corpus.

    Acceptance: all six tests green, both transports; live on the dev
    machine, the museum question asked with seeded episodes and a
    stubbed venue tool produces the conflict-aware recommendation with
    the progress line spoken, and its total time recorded against the
    deadline. Out of scope: worker models, a planner completion ahead
    of ordinary turns, writes inside the loop, a readability extractor
    for web pages (its own S item once websearch returns structured
    data), memory-first ordering of lookups (folded into the
    pre-filtered tool order, not a separate mechanism). Checks: the
    named suites, then the full exit gate.

Objective: per companion, prove the adapter carries the companion's voice without moving the substance, the cost, or tool calling. Build `backend/scripts/bench/style-adapter.ts` on `steering-spike.ts`'s runner (its thirty spoken turns, one conversation) and `written-set.ts`'s twenty-two rows and scorer, live on tier 1 against a hand-spawned engine on a spare port (the spike's own operator pattern; never the shared 8787 hub or 8788 engine), three seeded runs per arm: A floor (identity only, no adapter), B shipped (the real `contextToMessages()` composition, no adapter), C adapter (B's prompt byte-identical, `lora: [{id, scale: 1.0}]`), D vector (informational: `llama-cvector-generator` on this companion's own `examples` against neutral rewrites, `--control-vector`, the spike's identity-only prompt), E strength (informational: scale 0.5 and 1.5). Recorded per row and arm: predicted tokens, headings and lists, lowercase, the self-description check, contraction count, the companion's marker count (tokens in its `examples` absent from `default`'s), the five written fact answers, decode tokens per second, `cached_tokens`, the persona judge's relative score on the spoken set (trend only). Then `scripts/bench/tool-calling.ts` at 10 repeats with the adapter on. Pass bar per companion, all on arm C, exactly as dev.md states it: tokens within 0.85x-1.15x of B on at least 18 of 22 written rows with B's structure kept, 0 lowercase, 0 self-description, the five facts right; formal gives zero contractions on all 52 rows, casual a contraction on at least 24 of 30 spoken turns, frequent a marker on at least 18 of 30 spoken and 11 of 22 written, none gives no other companion's marker, every companion's written marker count above B's; turns 21-30 hold the voice checks within two turns of turns 1-10; the tool bench holds every positive and negative of the no-adapter run; decode at or above 0.9x of B; the one-slot companion-switch prefix re-evaluation recorded as a number. Mirror: `persona-eval.ts`'s string checks, `written-set.ts`'s table, `conversationScore.ts` (one scorer, never a second). Acceptance: the table per companion and arm in dev.md, each companion marked pass or fail against every line, arm D's result written beside C for the record; a failing companion ships no adapter and the miss is reported as a corpus or brief finding, never a lowered line. Out of scope: any hub runtime code, tuning the bar. Exit: the dev.md tables; the scripted mode of the bench green under `bash scripts/check.sh`. **Reading per shape (VOICE-CLASS-01, 2026-09-29, dev.md "VOICE-CLASS-01 design pass"):** every written row is classified by arm B's own reply with the corpus builder's `replyShape` (a heading, a list marker or more than two paragraphs is document-shaped); the substance line (the token band, B's structure kept, the five facts, lowercase, self-description) reads the whole reply on every row, unchanged; the voice lines (the marker count, contractions, formal's zero contractions) read the frame (`splitFrame`'s opener and closer) on a document-shaped row and the whole reply on a conversational one. The bar's numbers do not move; a companion is not failed for a contraction the bare model wrote inside a body the adapter was trained to copy, and gets no voice credit inside that body either. The table records each written row's shape beside its arm-C results. **Built and run 2026-09-29 (Sonnet):** `backend/scripts/bench/style-adapter.ts` built exactly to spec (byte-identical B/C/E replay via a capture proxy against `runTurnNext()`, never a hand-approximated prompt); `lora` wired into `llm.ts`'s `LlmCompleteOptions` with no other code path needed. Only decode cost clears, on every companion. This is the corpus's own already-disclosed finding (STYLE-CORPUS-02/STYLE-TRAIN-01: drop rate never cleared 20%, trained at 50/25 scale not 400/200) proving out at the gate, not a bench defect - reported as a corpus/brief finding per the row's own text, no line lowered. Arm D skipped (informational only, coordinator's own call - training four more control vectors for adapters that already fail everything else closes nothing). Full tables, the tool-calling comparison, the switch-cost number (9.77x the no-switch prompt time), and three real operational findings (a capture-proxy streaming bug, a residual intermittent stream failure mitigated by a retry, and a runaway-generation risk fixed with a token cap) are in dev.md's own "STYLE-BENCH-01" section. DONE: Commit 6e0fde79 (Add i18n scaffolding with Lingui); frontend/src/i18n.ts and frontend/src/locales exist; @lingui 6.6.0 still in frontend/package.json.

- [x] **i18n scaffolding for the shell, kit, and core pages, done**
      (session E step 8, 2026-09-06) - a narrower, more tractable slice
      of the item above (package/skill strings stay that item's own
      problem). Decided by the design-resolver agent against
      `getmaipai/.github/docs/ENGINEERING.md`'s real "Language and
      locale" rule ("UI strings live in a per-package message catalog;
      English is required") and the real, already-existing
      `household.locale` setting (`backend/src/settings/coreKeys.ts`,
      `range.options: ["en-US", "en-GB"]`) - the resolved
      `purring-chasing-noodle.md` ("plan 6.7") seed document is
      confirmed gone from every getmaipai repo, so the decision is
      grounded in what is actually real and checked in, not a document
      that no longer exists anywhere.

      **Library: Lingui** (`@lingui/core`, `@lingui/react`,
      `@lingui/cli`, `@lingui/vite-plugin`, all `6.6.0`), catalogs as
      `.po` files under `frontend/src/locales/<locale>/messages.po`,
      loaded eagerly (two small catalogs, no lazy-loading complexity
      worth adding yet) and activated from `household.locale` once
      settings load (`App.tsx`, `frontend/src/i18n.ts`) - the pre-auth
      SignIn screen has no household to read a preference from yet, so
      it stays on the source locale (`en-US`) by design, not a gap.

      **The macro transform (`<Trans>`/`t` from `@lingui/react/macro`/
      `@lingui/core/macro`) does not work in this repo and is not
      used** - a real toolchain incompatibility found live, not a design
      choice: Lingui's own documented Vite+React setup wires the macro
      through `@vitejs/plugin-react`'s `babel.plugins` option, but the
      version installed here (`@vitejs/plugin-react@6.1.1`) dropped
      Babel entirely for its own JSX transform (`oxc-transform-react`
      now) and its `Options` type has no `babel` property at all -
      passing it anyway silently did nothing. Every macro call then fell
      through to the macro package's own runtime guard, which throws
      ("executed outside the context of compilation") the instant React
      renders one - this broke the ENTIRE app (a blank page, 0 headings,
      a real `pageerror`) since the affected component was `Shell.tsx`'s
      nav rail, present on every signed-in route. Not caught by
      `bunx tsc --noEmit` (no type error - the option is accepted,
      just silently ignored) or by the first several `bun run a11y`
      passes (their own output was piped through `tail -N`, which
      truncated away the actual per-route failures and left only a
      misleadingly clean-looking tail); caught by grepping the built
      bundle directly for known UI strings ("Chat", "Settings",
      "Household") and finding every single one absent despite the
      bundle containing real React runtime code, then confirmed with a
      direct Playwright check showing the exact runtime error. Fixed by
      dropping macros and using Lingui's plain runtime API instead -
      `<Trans id="..." message="..." />` from the real `@lingui/react`
      (not `/macro`) for JSX, `i18n._("...")` from `@/i18n` for the one
      non-JSX (tooltip) case - which needs no Babel pass at all;
      `lingui extract` finds both forms equally well (marked
      `js-lingui-explicit-id` in the generated catalogs). Re-enabling
      macros later needs either a Babel-based React plugin variant or
      `@lingui/swc-plugin`, neither installed now.

      **Extracted a small, real, working slice**, not a full sweep:
      `Shell.tsx`'s "Search" nav row and `HomePage.tsx`'s "Today"
      heading, both real, both loadable in both catalogs, proving the
      whole pipeline (extraction, catalog loading, `household.locale`
      selection) end to end. A full sweep of every hardcoded string in
      `frontend/src` is tracked below as its own item - doing it in the
      same step as standing up the whole system for the first time would
      conflate "does the plumbing work" with "is every string moved."
      **Deferred, documented, not built**: the far surface's type scale
      per script (`.surface-far` in `tokens.css` stays Latin-only,
      commented as such) - `household.locale`'s own option list is
      Latin-script-only today, so there is no non-Latin locale to verify
      a script-specific scale against, and this org's testing standard
      ("verified means exercised for real") rules out building something
      unverifiable.

DONE: Commit aa206e16 (Lane 10 item 2: real code-splitting for the frontend shell chunk); frontend/src/App.tsx has lazyNamed; docs/assets/screens/lazy-route-skeleton.png exists.

- [x] **Real code-splitting for the frontend shell chunk** (M) - found
      at Session E's own step 10 wrap-up merge (2026-09-06): the main
      chunk crossed the PWA plugin's default 2 MiB precache ceiling once
      everything Wave 2 merged in landed together (real growth, not a
      broken build - `vite build`'s own "chunks larger than 500 kB"
      warning had already been firing for a while before this). Worked
      around for now by raising `workbox.
      maximumFileSizeToCacheInBytes` to 5 MiB in `vite.config.ts` so the
      app-shell service worker keeps precaching the real shell in full,
      rather than silently dropping it from the one cache it exists to
      populate - not a fix for the underlying size. `vite build`'s own
      suggestion (`dynamic import()`, `rolldownOptions.output.
      codeSplitting`) is the real fix, unexplored so far.

      **Status, done 2026-09-13 (lane 10 item 2)**: route-level
      `React.lazy()` (`App.tsx`'s `lazyNamed()`) for every app but Home
      and Chat (docs/dev/session-b.md, "Lane 10 item 2," has the reasoning
      for keeping those two eager). Entry chunk 2,103.55 kB → 1,891.89 kB
      raw (485.76 kB → 429.02 kB gzip), 1 JS chunk → 39 (Rolldown's own
      automatic vendor splitting, not just this step's 15 route
      boundaries). That's back under Workbox's default 2 MiB ceiling with
      about 205 KB (9.8%) to spare, so the `maximumFileSizeToCacheInBytes`
      override is removed entirely rather than lowered to some other
      number. `RouteSkeleton` (new, `kit/primitives/`) is the Suspense
      fallback; a real in-app navigation never shows it at all
      (react-router-dom's `Link` wraps navigation in `startTransition`,
      which keeps the previous page live rather than flash a loader), but
      a fresh load straight at a lazy route's own URL does, screenshotted
      and opened (`docs/assets/screens/lazy-route-skeleton.png`).

set with anything below bronze, which today it structurally can't check
